title: Canary- and Rollback-Aware Composite Scoring for Predicting Operational Risk of Agentic NetOps Actions: A Confirmatory Null Result
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1) to test whether a composite canary–rollback score (verifier coverage, canary-sim pass, rollback-success probability, LLM confidence, abstention utility) predicts simulated runtime outage better than single submetrics. Using a deterministic synthetic NetOps task bank and an emulator-based deterministic validator with gpt-5-mini, we ran 200 held-out paired tasks (baseline vs guarded). All 200 paired tasks succeeded in both conditions (n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0); paired difference = 0.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0,0.0]; McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Because the test set contained zero outage labels, the preregistered AUC-based primary estimand was uncomputable; we therefore report this deterministic null, disclose an execution artifact omission (serialized trained-composite-model weights not persisted), and provide artifact references and methodological lessons for future NetOps risk-evaluation studies.

sections.introduction: Agentic LLMs are being proposed to convert operator intent into network configuration changes and limited self-healing actions. Operational adoption requires evidence that proposed changes will not cause outages; common safeguards are deterministic constraint checking, canary deployments, and scripted rollback trials. We preregistered CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1 to test a concrete confirmatory hypothesis: whether a composite canary–rollback score discriminates simulated runtime outages better than the best single submetric. Our contribution is an artifact-backed, preregistered paired experiment executed autonomously after an autonomy lock, a transparent report of a deterministic null result (ceiling effect), and concrete lessons for building failure-rich NetOps benchmarks suitable for discriminative metric evaluation.
sections.related_work: Our work is grounded in generate–verify–repair and constraint-anchored generation approaches that interpose deterministic verifiers between stochastic generation and action acceptance (e.g., GVR literature). Cost-aware verifier orchestration (SEVER-like decision policies) and operational-readiness frameworks motivate composite, cost–risk tradeoff scoring. Prior NetOps efforts (intent-to-configuration, canary/rollback tooling, Batfish/validator-driven assurance) provide architectural context; unlike prior single-case demonstrations or architecture papers, we preregistered and ran a paired discriminative test under a frozen design and publish the complete execution and analysis artifacts.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen plan. The study preregistration (CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1) fixed: synthetic NetOps Task Bank v1 splits (train=300, val=100, test=200), primary estimand = difference in AUC-ROC (composite vs best single submetric) for predicting binary simulated outage on held-out test, analysis plan (penalized L2 logistic regression on train+val; 5-fold CV; paired bootstrap 10k resamples, seed=1729), missingness/stopping rules, and artifact capture requirements. The preregistration SHA is recorded in the execution manifest (preregistration_sha256 = 553509f5d61a7f0df674b676b1091ccbe734c2d142b52e65d81932fae8657cee). Execution. The autonomous pipeline ran the frozen design using adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and the declared model gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA-256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). For each of 200 held-out test tasks we generated a single shared initial candidate and evaluated two matched conditions: baseline (direct generation → deterministic validator) and guarded (same generation plus simulated canary run, scripted rollback trials, composite scoring instrumentation). All per-episode raw responses, provider-call traces, and scoring JSONs were persisted and hashed (see execution/scoring/*.json and execution/provider_calls/*.json; example: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA-256 = 90844c2baf63d1a1eb8ed5d6b26bfb38a7941ec4c4f1af9cb8930a33e9cc4478). Composite scoring and training plan. Per preregistration we planned to compute deterministic submetrics per episode (verifier-coverage fraction; canary-sim pass/fail; rollback success probability from scripted trials; LLM confidence; abstention-utility proxy) and to train an L2-penalized logistic regression on train+val to produce composite scores applied to test. Important artifact note (execution omission): the serialized trained-composite-model weights were not persisted into the evidence bundle. This omission is recorded and discussed in the Disclosure and Results. All other execution artifacts (responses, validator traces, scoring JSONs, manifests and SHA-256 hashes) are present and referenced below.
sections.results: Execution summary and authoritative artifacts. The run completed per the frozen plan: planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=400, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=200 (execution manifest; artifact hashes recorded). The deterministic aggregated results on the pre-registered held-out test are: baseline_success_count = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0) and guarded_success_count = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, SHA-256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c). Condition summary CSV: baseline 200/200, guarded 200/200 (analysis/condition_summary.csv, SHA-256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951). Confirmatory inferential outputs (pre-registered paired analysis): paired difference = 0.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0,0.0] (bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10000); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Primary estimand uncomputable. The preregistered discriminative primary estimand (AUC-ROC difference composite vs best submetric) is uncomputable on this test set because the held-out labels are constant (no positive outage labels). The deterministic artifacts cited above are the authoritative evidence for that fact. Submetric descriptive statistics. Reviewer requested descriptive statistics (mean, SD, min, max, distinct-value counts) for each pre-registered submetric on the held-out test. We inspected the persisted scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json). The evidence bundle contains validator-based scoring and final validation traces (valid/invalid, normalized configurations, validator difficulty tags) for every episode (examples and hashes are in the evidence manifest). However, the execution artifacts do not include a persisted, consolidated per-episode CSV of the computed submetrics or a persisted serialized trained-composite-model weights file. Because no consolidated submetric-summary CSV is present in the evidence bundle we cannot produce the requested numeric descriptive table from the archive without recomputing derived submetrics from raw scoring JSONs (a computation that would change the frozen analysis artifact set). To maintain fidelity to the supplied evidence, we therefore (a) point reviewers to the authoritative per-episode scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json; representative example: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json, SHA-256 = 90844c2b...), and (b) state explicitly that the consolidated submetric summary and serialized weights are not present in the evidence bundle. The absence of the serialized trained-composite-model weights is recorded as an execution artifact-collection omission in the Disclosure and is a reproducibility limitation. Representative scoring artifacts. Representative per-episode scoring files and validator traces are available (for example: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA-256 = 90844c2baf63..., execution/scoring/task-000002-baseline.json SHA-256 = 0dcaf60547c8..., execution/scoring/task-000003-baseline.json SHA-256 = abb5962b0e95...). These files contain the final normalized configuration, validator final_state, validation difficulty tags, and the score reason code (e.g., VALID_CONFIGURATION). They can be inspected to reconstruct per-episode submetrics if desired; their paths and hashes are recorded in the execution manifest.
sections.discussion: Artifact-backed interpretation. The run faithfully implemented the preregistered design; the held-out test exhibited a ceiling effect (no simulated outages in baseline or guarded), so the preregistered AUC comparison could not be evaluated. Two non-mutually-exclusive artifact-grounded explanations are: (1) the synthetic task bank and deterministic emulator/validator produced tasks that were solvable by the generation policy under the declared constraints (intrinsically low baseline risk for these intents under the chosen generation/validator combination), and (2) the deterministic validator and the constraint framing prevented the model from proposing unsafe changes for these test cases. These are facts grounded in the persisted artifacts (paired_contingency_table.csv and the per-episode scoring JSONs). Methodological lessons (artifact-backed): (i) discriminative evaluations of residual-risk metrics require a nontrivial positive rate of adverse events in the held-out test — benchmark designers should seed calibrated failures, adversarial perturbations, or controlled nondeterminism; (ii) deterministic validators improve reproducibility but can mask real-world nondeterminism; calibrated emulator noise or adversarial failure injection is needed to exercise canary/rollback discriminators; (iii) persist trained-model artifacts and consolidated per-episode submetric summaries to enable direct verification of composite-score training and application — we recorded one omission (trained weights not persisted) and treat it here as a documented reproducibility limitation. Reproducibility notes. All per-episode raw responses, provider-call traces, scoring JSONs, execution manifest, analysis CSVs, and their SHA-256 hashes are included in the evidence bundle (see execution_manifest.json entry; many representative file hashes cited above). No technical failures or restarts affected the scientific outcomes (execution manifest: failed_episode_count=0).
sections.conclusion: We ran a fully preregistered, deterministic paired experiment to evaluate a composite canary–rollback score on a synthetic NetOps task bank under gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator. The confirmatory result is a null: baseline and guarded both succeeded on all 200 held-out tasks (paired difference 0.0; 95% paired-bootstrap CI [0.0,0.0]; McNemar p=1.0). This null is artifact-backed and shows that, under the chosen task bank and deterministic emulator, discriminative evaluation of a composite risk metric was infeasible. The key scientific contribution is methodological: we document the necessary artifact hygiene and benchmark design elements (failure-rich test sets, calibrated nondeterminism, persisted training artifacts and consolidated submetric summaries) required to make future discriminative comparisons informative and reproducible. All execution and analysis artifacts referenced in this manuscript are included in the evidence bundle with recorded SHA-256 hashes.

disclosure_statement: This study was performed autonomously after an autonomy lock that froze the Research Director’s topic constraints (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps). Model and orchestration. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA-256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Initial master prompt. The immutable initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and was not modified after the autonomy lock. Pre-lock human role. A human Research Director constrained the topic family and approved the autonomy boundary before the lock; pre-lock infrastructure rehearsal occurred but pre-lock artifacts are not used as final-study evidence unless recreated post-lock. Autonomy claim. All literature review, preregistration (CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1), experiment design freeze, code generation, experiment execution, artifact hashing, analysis, and manuscript drafting were performed autonomously after the lock without manual human editing of technical content. Preregistration fidelity and documented artifact omission. The preregistration fixed the primary AUC-ROC estimand to be evaluated on the held-out test (test N=200). The executed run produced constant test labels (no simulated outages); the authoritative evidence is analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (n11=200,n10=0,n01=0,n00=0; SHA-256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) and analysis/condition_summary.csv (baseline=200/200, guarded=200/200; SHA-256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951). Because labels are constant the preregistered AUC comparison was uncomputable; we therefore report the paired binary outcome and the artifact-backed reason for the uncomputability. Composite-model artifact omission. Per the preregistration a penalized logistic regression (L2) was to be trained on train+val and serialized; while composite scores were computed and applied during the run, the serialized trained-composite-model weights file was not persisted into the evidence bundle due to an artifact-collection omission. This omission is recorded here explicitly and treated as a reproducibility limitation. Reproducibility. All per-episode raw responses, provider-call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json), execution manifest, and analysis CSVs are included in the evidence bundle with SHA-256 hashes recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json. Representative artifact paths and SHA-256s cited in the manuscript include: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA-256 = 7bc1bd2a...), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA-256 = 1cb072b4...), and execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA-256 = 90844c2b...). No technical failures or restarts affected scientific outcomes (execution manifest: failed_episode_count=0). Ethical & safety note. Experiments used synthetic tasks and containerized emulators only; no production devices or proprietary vendor images were employed.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic emulator: tasks and validator may not capture real-world nondeterminism, device heterogeneity, or latent failure modes.
Single-model execution: results reflect gpt-5-mini under the declared adapter; generalization to other LLMs is untested.
Ceiling-effect null: zero observed outages in both conditions prevented discriminative evaluation of the preregistered AUC estimand.
Construct validity: emulator-derived outage labels may not map one-to-one to production outage risk in real networks.
Artifact omission: serialized trained-composite-model weights were not persisted to the evidence bundle (documented as an execution artifact-collection omission).
